classifications.reasoning: Rule detects attempts to access ASP files via Alternate Data Streams (::DATA), a known IIS exploit technique for source code disclosure against public-facing web servers.
Rule matches requests for .bat files in CGI directories, corresponding to multiple CVEs (1999-0233, 2002-0061, 2019-0232) that allow remote command execution via vulnerable web applications.
Rule detects access to .cnf configuration files, exploiting CVE-2002-1717 which allows remote attackers to read sensitive configuration files on IIS servers.
Rule matches the specific query parameters used in CVE-2000-0302 (Index Server ISAPI extension) to disclose ASP source code via a public-facing IIS web application.
Rule detects the .htw?CiWebHitsFile pattern used in CVE-2000-0942 to exploit the IIS Index Server hit-highlighting feature for ASP source disclosure.
Rule targets access to CGImail.exe, a vulnerable CGI script (CVE-2000-0726) that allows remote command execution on IIS servers.
Rule detects requests for ctguestb.idc, a sample IDC file associated with CVE-1999-0874 (JET VBA) that can be exploited to access database content via the web server.
Rule matches access to details.idc, another sample file linked to CVE-1999-0874, indicating exploitation attempts against the JET VBA component in IIS.

Rule detects access to the MSProxy w3proxy.dll component; while this could indicate proxy usage (T1090), the reference is a Microsoft KB article and the exact adversary intent (proxy vs. exploit) is ambiguous from the signature alone.
Rule specifically matches the sensepost.exe filename, a known web shell deployed on compromised IIS servers for persistent command execution.
Rule detects requests for _vti_inf.html, a FrontPage Server Extensions file that discloses server version and configuration information, consistent with file and directory discovery.
Rule targets the achg.htr password change page, which is associated with CVE-1999-0407 allowing unauthorized password changes — an account manipulation technique.
Rule matches access to adctest.asp, a sample ADC/RDS test page that can reveal database connectivity details; primarily an information disclosure / file discovery vector.
Rule detects access to the /iisadmin virtual directory, which is linked to CVE-1999-1538 allowing remote administration and exploitation of IIS.
Rule matches the default.htm page under the IIS admin scripts directory, another vector for the same IIS admin vulnerability (CVE-1999-1538).
Rule detects the ism.dll?http/dir exploit string used in CVE-1999-1538 and CVE-2000-0630 to enumerate directories and execute commands via the IIS admin interface.
Rule matches the anot.htr page (part of the IIS password change functionality) also covered by CVE-1999-0407, used for unauthorized account manipulation.
Rule detects the trailing dot (.asp.) technique used to retrieve ASP source code instead of executing it, a file/directory discovery method.
Rule matches a typo and continue. The rule matches a URL-encoded search for *.asp files (|23| is #), indicating active enumeration of ASP files on the server.
Rule detects access to bdir.htr, a directory browsing script that can list directory contents, facilitating file and directory discovery.
Same as previous rule but for the root-level bdir.htr; also enables directory listing and file discovery.
Rule matches the carbo.dll ISAPI extension with icatcommand parameter, exploiting CVE-1999-1069 for remote code execution on IIS.
Rule detects the string cmd.exe in HTTP requests, a common indicator of attempts to execute Windows command shell via web application vulnerabilities.
Rule matches .cmd?& pattern, another variant of command execution attempts against IIS web applications.
Rule targets the Exair code browser sample (codebrws.asp) which can disclose source code and directory structure, a file/directory discovery technique.
